content.comment_body: I've noticed there's a simple sample program in the manual to get a program's cycle time, but is there a way to calculate it without relying on that method?

It's not possible to calculate this directly, because [company_name] does not provide details about the processing time needed for individual blocks. They only mention that the execution time is under 0.1 ms.

I recall seeing a chart a long time ago in one of the older manuals for [product_name] that outlined execution times for specific blocks. Has that information been removed? Is there a pre-made test program available in a library somewhere? I don't have the time to learn how to create a program on the PLC from scratch.
Cycle time measurement by [product_name]? That's news to me. I only recall documentation relating to the memory requirements for individual blocks.
Maybe I'm mistaken and was thinking about block memory usage, sorry. Is there any chance of a library program I could add that shows the cycle time?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are searching for a convenient solution to check program cycle time for [product_name] hardware, ideally without manual coding or relying solely on sample programs. They remember past documentation providing specific execution times for blocks, but note that such details are now missing. There is interest in ready-to-use library programs or features that automate cycle time measurement.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want easy and direct access to cycle time monitoring, ideally through a built-in library program or feature, rather than needing to develop manual solutions.
